segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Smaller or lower-priority Node built-in modules, grouped here rather than given a full page each. Split out to its own page (rather than [PROCESS-CLI.md](PROCESS-CLI.md)) once it's substantial enough to need one.

notes: Surface: `.parse`, `.stringify`, `.escape`, `.unescape`, `.unescapeBuffer`, `.encode`, `.decode` — Node's `lib/querystring.js` in TypeScript ([ADR-01173](../adr/ADR-01173.md))
`.parse` returns a null-prototype object (a repeated key's values in an array), honours `sep`/`eq`/`maxKeys`/`decodeURIComponent`, and doesn't strip a leading `?` (unlike `new URLSearchParams(str)`)
`.stringify` takes an object (an array value repeats its key), with `sep`/`eq`/`encodeURIComponent`

caveats: No `assert.CallTracker` (deprecated in Node, DEP0173)
Deep equality does not compare symbol-keyed properties, and a failure diff does not invoke getters (Node's `getters: true`)
An uncaught `AssertionError` prints `Uncaught: <message>`; Node prints `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: <message>`, its stack and its properties
notes: Node's lib/assert.js in TypeScript (`lib/node/assert.ts`, with `AssertionError`, the Myers diff and `isDeepStrictEqual` ported alongside): every assertion, `rejects`/`doesNotReject`, `partialDeepStrictEqual`, the `Assert` class, and `assert/strict`; messages, diffs and `ok`'s quoted call source match Node's ([ADR-01288](../adr/ADR-01288.md))
Colours follow stderr as Node's do: plain unless it is a terminal that shows them

caveats: A failing test's details omit Node's `test at <file>:<line>:<col>` line and the stack: the error prints as `Name [code]: message`
No `mock.*`, `run()`, snapshots, concurrency, timeouts, `t.signal`/`t.assert`, or `only` filtering
The spec reporter prints without colors on a terminal (Node colors it); no other reporter
notes: `node:test` is Node's runner in TypeScript (`lib/node/test.ts`, [ADR-01282](../adr/ADR-01282.md)): tests run after the module, one at a time in registration order, a suite's function when it is registered; `test`/`it`, `describe`/`suite`, `test.skip`/`todo`/`only`, the options `skip`/`todo`/`plan`, TestContext `t.test`/`t.skip`/`t.todo`/`t.diagnostic`/`t.plan`/`t.name`/`t.fullName` and its hooks, module hooks `before`/`after`/`beforeEach`/`afterEach`; the spec reporter's output and summary as Node prints them, held until the event loop turns as Node's reporter stream delivers them; exit code 1 on a failure

The bare `test` specifier is Node's own test-suite helpers (Node's `test/common`, `lib/node/test_common.ts`): `mustCall`/`mustCallAtLeast` (checked at exit: `Mismatched <name> function calls. Expected exactly N, actual M.`), `mustSucceed` (asserts no error, then calls with the rest), `mustNotCall`, `expectsError`, `expectWarning`, `skip` (`1..0 # Skipped: …`, exit 0), and the platform probes — alongside the runner's functions

caveats: `promisify(f) === f` is false for an already-promisified `f`: a function unboxed from `any` is a new thunk

`.inspect` renders through the compiler's inspector: `depth`, `compact` (a number or `false`; `true` is treated as 3), `sorted` (not a comparator), `breakLength` and `maxArrayLength` apply; `colors`, `showHidden`, `getters`, `maxStringLength`, `numericSeparator` and `[inspect.custom]` methods do not, so `%o` shows no hidden properties
No `inherits`, `parseArgs`, `MIMEType`, `getCallSites`, `transferableAbortSignal`, `parseEnv` or `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` through `util` (they are globals); `debuglog`'s logger is typed `any`
notes: Node's lib/util.js in TypeScript (`lib/node/util.ts`, [ADR-01289](../adr/ADR-01289.md)): `format`/`formatWithOptions` (Node's own specifier walk: a runtime format string, `%s` calling a program's own `toString`), `inspect` with `inspect.custom`/`colors`/`styles`/`defaultOptions`, `isDeepStrictEqual`, `callbackify`, `deprecate`, `debuglog`/`debug` (`NODE_DEBUG`), `stripVTControlCharacters`, `toUSVString`, `getSystemErrorName`/`Message`/`Map`, `styleText` (plain unless the stream shows colours), `types`, `aborted`, and the deprecated `isArray`
`.promisify` is Node's `lib/internal/util.js` ([ADR-01172](../adr/ADR-01172.md)), with `promisify.custom` ([ADR-01236](../adr/ADR-01236.md))

caveats: BlockList, SocketAddress and happy-eyeballs address selection (`autoSelectFamily`) are not ported
On Windows the TCP handles are compile-checked, not yet run
notes: Node's `lib/net.js` ported to TypeScript (`lib/node/net.ts`) over native TCP handles on the event loop: Socket (a Duplex — back-pressure, `'drain'`, pause/resume, `setEncoding`, `setTimeout`, `ref`/`unref`), Server (`listen` by port/host/backlog/options or a Unix-socket path, dual-stack `::` by default, `'listening'`/`'error'` on the next tick, `maxConnections`, `getConnections`), `connect`/`createConnection` (port, options, `{ path }`), `isIP`/`isIPv4`/`isIPv6`; errors built as Node builds them ([ADR-01170](../adr/ADR-01170.md))

caveats: Sends are synchronous (a full send buffer is waited out), so `getSendQueueSize()`/`getSendQueueCount()` are always 0
The `lookup`, `receiveBlockList`/`sendBlockList` options, `bind({ fd })` and cluster-shared sockets are not ported
Windows: the TTL and multicast options and membership apply to `udp4` sockets only, and that path is compile-checked, not run
notes: Node's lib/dgram.js in TypeScript ([ADR-01263](../adr/ADR-01263.md)) over datagram handles in the pool reactor: `udp4`/`udp6`, `createSocket(type | options, listener?)`, `bind` (resolving its address; `'listening'`), `send` in every form (offset/length, a list, before the bind completes — queued), `connect`/`disconnect`/`remoteAddress`, `close`, `address`, `setBroadcast`/`setTTL`/`setMulticastTTL`/`setMulticastLoopback`/`setMulticastInterface`, `addMembership`/`dropMembership`, buffer sizes, `ref`/`unref`

`'message'` receives a Buffer and `{ address, family, port, size }`; the socket exists once bound, as libuv's does (an option before the bind is `EBADF`); Node's error codes (`ERR_SOCKET_BAD_TYPE`, `ERR_SOCKET_ALREADY_BOUND`, `ERR_SOCKET_DGRAM_NOT_RUNNING`, …)

caveats: OpenSSL-only (libssl) — a `-crypto=commoncrypto` build using `tls` is a clean compile error (Mac's CommonCrypto has no TLS API)
Session resumption, OCSP, renegotiation, PSK and `getPeerCertificate()`'s certificate object are not ported
On Windows the TCP handles are compile-checked, not yet run
notes: Node's `_tls_wrap` shape in TypeScript (`lib/node/tls.ts`): a TLSSocket is a net.Socket whose handle carries a non-blocking OpenSSL session — `tls.connect` (`servername`, `rejectUnauthorized`, `ca`/`cert`/`key`, ALPN; `'secureConnect'`, `authorized`/`authorizationError`, Node's verify error codes and messages), `tls.createServer` (`'secureConnection'`, `'tlsClientError'`), `createSecureContext`, `getProtocol`/`getCipher` ([ADR-01170](../adr/ADR-01170.md))

caveats: A c-ares error has no `errno` key (Node's has `errno: undefined`): the error layout's `errno` slot is numeric
The Windows server discovery and client are compile-checked only
notes: Node's lib/dns.js in TypeScript: `lookup` (`all`/`family`/`hints`/`order`/`verbatim`), `lookupService`, `resolve`/`resolve4`/`resolve6` (with `ttl`)/`resolveMx`/`Txt`/`Srv`/`Ns`/`Cname`/`Ptr`/`Soa`/`Naptr`/`Caa`/`Tlsa`/`Any`, `reverse`, `Resolver` (`timeout`/`tries`/`maxTimeout`, `setServers`/`getServers`, `cancel`, `setLocalAddress`), `get`/`setDefaultResultOrder`, the error-code constants and `dns.promises` ([ADR-01294](../adr/ADR-01294.md))

`lookup` and `lookupService` are `getaddrinfo`/`getnameinfo` on the thread pool, as libuv's; the `resolve*` family is a native DNS client standing in for c-ares (UDP with TCP on truncation, the system's servers, c-ares' statuses), its records shaped as cares_wrap's parsers shape them
Verified against Node on the Mac (Apple Silicon) and on Linux (Docker, glibc/arm64)

caveats: Brotli and Zstd load the system libbrotli/libzstd at run time (Node bundles them): where they are missing, making a Brotli or Zstd stream is `ERR_ZLIB_INITIALIZATION_FAILED`
Compressed bytes are the system libz's, which can differ from Node's bundled zlib at the same level (each inflates the other's)
A `*Sync` call with `info: true` is typed `{ buffer, engine }` by an extra overload (@types types it `Buffer`)
notes: Node's lib/zlib.js in TypeScript (`lib/node/zlib.ts`, [ADR-01296](../adr/ADR-01296.md)): `Deflate`/`Inflate`/`Gzip`/`Gunzip`/`DeflateRaw`/`InflateRaw`/`Unzip` streams and their `create*` functions, the one-shot methods (callback and `*Sync`), `crc32`, `constants` and `codes`, with every zlib option, `params`/`flush`/`reset`/`close` and `bytesWritten`
A native handle per stream (`klainzlib.c`, node_zlib.cc's `ZlibContext`) whose writes run on the thread pool; `-lz` only for a program that uses it

`BrotliCompress`/`BrotliDecompress`/`ZstdCompress`/`ZstdDecompress`, `brotli*`/`zstd*` one-shots and `create*`, with `params`, dictionaries and `pledgedSrcSize`, and Node's error codes (`ERR_BROTLI_INVALID_PARAM`, `ERR__ERROR_FORMAT_*`, `ZSTD_error_*`) ([ADR-01305](../adr/ADR-01305.md))
Input may be a Buffer/TypedArray, ArrayBuffer, DataView, or string (UTF-8); output is always a Buffer
Surface: `vm.Script`, sandboxed `eval`-like execution
Same fundamental blocker as the already-tracked bare `eval()` — see [GLOBAL-FUNCTIONS.md](GLOBAL-FUNCTIONS.md). Opt-in embedded-engine path scoped in [TDD-00046](../tdd/TDD-00046.md), not started

Node's lib/diagnostics_channel.js in TypeScript ([ADR-01254](../adr/ADR-01254.md)): `channel`/`subscribe`/`unsubscribe`/`hasSubscribers`/`tracingChannel`, the `Channel` class (`publish` of any value, `subscribe`/`unsubscribe`, `bindStore`/`unbindStore`/`runStores`, `hasSubscribers`, `name`) and `TracingChannel` (`traceSync`/`tracePromise`/`traceCallback`, `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` of the five events)
A subscriber's throw is reported on the next tick — the process `'uncaughtException'` event when something listens, else fatal — and the other subscribers still run, as in Node

caveats: `http.request(new URL(…))` is not accepted — a `string | URL | options` parameter is a union code generation cannot tell apart ([BACKLOG](../BACKLOG.md))
notes: Node's `_http_agent`/`_http_client` in TypeScript (`lib/node/internal_http.ts`) over `net`: ClientRequest (an OutgoingMessage — chunked bodies, `'response'`/`'socket'`/`'information'`/`'upgrade'`/`'error'`, `abort`/`destroy`/`setTimeout`), Agent with keep-alive pooling (`http.globalAgent` keeps sockets alive and unref'd, as Node 19+), `IncomingMessage` responses as Readables ([ADR-01170](../adr/ADR-01170.md))

caveats: Same client limit as `http` for a `URL` argument ([BACKLOG](../BACKLOG.md))
notes: `https.createServer` is a `tls.Server` running the http module's connection handling; `https.request`/`get`/`Agent`/`globalAgent` connect with `tls.connect` ([ADR-01170](../adr/ADR-01170.md))
Surface: re-exports: `ReadableStream`/`WritableStream`/`TransformStream`/`CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream`

The names bind as identity to the ambient WHATWG constructors that already exist — importing them is interchangeable with the globals ([ADR-00410](../adr/ADR-00410.md)); the queuing-strategy classes are not exported

caveats: `setupPrimary({ exec })` naming another file fails at `fork()` with `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_FORK_MODULE`: a worker is this compiled program, so there is no other script for it to run (a genuine impossibility of native compilation, [ADR-01015](../adr/ADR-01015.md))
`inspectPort` and the inspector flags are ignored: a compiled program has no inspector
A `dgram` socket bound in a worker binds on its own, not through the primary
Windows: a worker's `listen` has no handle to receive — descriptor passing over the fork channel is POSIX-only
notes: Node's lib/internal/cluster in TypeScript (`lib/node/cluster.ts`): workers are forks over the IPC channel; a worker's `net`/`http` server listens through the primary, which accepts and hands connections round (`SCHED_RR`, the POSIX default) or sends the listening socket to every worker (`SCHED_NONE`, `NODE_CLUSTER_SCHED_POLICY=none`); Worker and cluster-level events, `cluster.workers` keyed by id, `worker.disconnect()`/`kill()`, `cluster.disconnect(cb)`, `setupPrimary` and `settings` ([ADR-01302](../adr/ADR-01302.md))
`klain:http`'s `http.listen` in a cluster worker shares the port with `SO_REUSEPORT`, as `http.listen({ workers })` does

caveats: `respondWithFD`/`respondWithFile` read the whole file into memory before sending it, where Node streams it
`session.altsvc()`/`origin()` validate their arguments but send no frame
`setNextStreamID`/`setLocalWindowSize` validate their argument only
`session.socket` is the raw socket, not Node's Proxy that rejects the socket methods an h2 session owns
The `Http2ServerRequest`/`Http2ServerResponse` server options (subclasses) are ignored
`stream.write` has no backpressure: it always returns `true` and buffers
Most session tuning options (`maxSessionMemory`, `maxHeaderListPairs`, `paddingStrategy`, `peerMaxConcurrentStreams`, …) are accepted and ignored
notes: Node's lib/internal/http2 (core.js, compat.js, util.js) in TypeScript (`lib/node/http2.ts`) over an event-queue nghttp2 session per `Http2Session` (`http2src/h2node.c`): `createServer`/`createSecureServer` (ALPN, `allowHTTP1`), `connect` over h2c and TLS, the compat `(req, res)` and `'stream'` APIs, push streams, RST, settings, ping, goaway, trailers, stream/session timeouts ([ADR-01301](../adr/ADR-01301.md))
Transparent h2 without the `http2` import: `fetch` negotiates h2 over TLS (ALPN); `klain:http`'s `http.listen` serves h2c prior-knowledge alongside 1.1 ([ADR-00357](../adr/ADR-00357.md))

Node's `AsyncLocalStorage` and `AsyncResource` in TypeScript ([ADR-01257](../adr/ADR-01257.md)): the current async context is a frame mapping each store to its value, as Node's AsyncContextFrame; `run`/`exit`/`enterWith`/`getStore`/`disable`, the `name`/`defaultValue` options, static `bind`/`snapshot`, `AsyncResource`'s `runInAsyncScope`/`bind`/static `bind`

The frame propagates **across `await`** — the runtime keeps it in the coroutine task, and a spawned task inherits it ([ADR-00678](../adr/ADR-00678.md)) — and into promise reactions, `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`setImmediate`, `process.nextTick` and `queueMicrotask` callbacks scheduled inside `run(...)` ([ADR-00679](../adr/ADR-00679.md), [ADR-01257](../adr/ADR-01257.md))
`getStore()` on an unset/disabled store is a real `undefined` typed `T | undefined` ([ADR-00782](../adr/ADR-00782.md))
caveats: `createHook`, `executionAsyncId`, `triggerAsyncId` and `executionAsyncResource` are not exported; an `AsyncResource`'s `asyncId()` numbers resources in creation order, with no init/before/after/destroy lifecycle behind it
